Alex — thanks for the note and the PDF. Below is a concise packet we typically provide; I attached our availability runbook (redwood-availability-runbook.pdf), a sample Grafana invite text (grafana-invite.txt), and the metrics schema (redwood-metrics-schema.xlsx).

Quick answers (TL;DR):
- How we measure SLOs: availability SLOs are derived from per-route 5xx/timeout rates and a rolling-window success-rate computation at 1m/5m/1h granularity. Latency SLOs use p50/p95/p99 computed from sampled request traces. All aggregation is done in our telemetry pipeline (Prometheus -> Cortex -> long-term store).
- Monitoring & alerts: We maintain alerting rules tied to SLO burn rate and absolute thresholds (e.g., p95 > 800ms for web-api route for 5m). Burn-rate alerts trigger paging to on-call; softer alerts create Ops tickets and notify customer success.
- Customer metric access: Customers can be granted read-only dashboards in a per-account Grafana tenancy (no cross-customer visibility). We also provide an SLO report CSV export and a daily S3 snapshot on request.
- Exception requests: Exceptions (temporary SLO deviations) must be requested via the customer portal or via your Redwood CSM; they include justification, start/end times, and rollback plan. For procurement/legal, we can include an exception approval flow that requires product + security + legal sign-off for >72h exceptions.

Examples of when an exception is expected:
- Initial dedicated pool warm-up (first 48–72h) for new Dedicated customers
- Large model upgrade with expected warm caches during rollouts

Next steps: If you want, we can redline the questionnaire directly and provide a one-page summary to procurement. If Everest needs dashboard invites now, I can send a sample invite link (grafana-invite.txt) and add your monitoring contact.

Cheers,
Dylan Brooks
Head of Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-availability-runbook.pdf; grafana-invite.txt; redwood-metrics-schema.xlsx

Adding a couple of clarifications we should include in the procurement response (cc'd for transparency):

- Measurement windows: procurement frequently asks for the exact query semantics; the runbook includes the PromQL we use for availability and latency SLOs. For contracts we can include the canonical 30d rolling window for compliance checks, with 7d for short-term operational alerts.
- Data retention for SLO proofs: raw samples retained 90 days in hot storage, aggregated SLO metrics retained 2 years per enterprise offering. We can add this as a clause if Everest needs it in the MSA.
- Exception approval: for trial Dedicated customers (like early onboarding for EV-3421), we can pre-authorize a single 72h operational tolerance window without legal review — Product + Security approval only; anything beyond that triggers Legal. Flagged to Ben for commercial implications.

Finally, Dylan — please confirm the wording on the per-account Grafana tenancy (we shouldn't promise cross-account joins).

Laura Bennett
Director, Customer Success
Redwood Inference
